THIS AGREEMENT WILL DEVELOP AN APPROACH TO ASSESS WILDFIRE AND POST-FIRE FLOOD AND DEBRIS FLOW RISK FOR HISTORIC STRUCTURES AND ARCHEOLOGICAL SITES IN FIRE-PRONE AND IMPACTED LANDSCAPES IN NEW MEXICO. THESE SITES ARE POPULAR RECREATIONAL DESTINATIONS AND EXIST IN AREAS WITH HIGH RISK OF WILDFIRE. ACTIVITIES ASSOCIATED WITH THIS AGREEMENT WILL HELP IDENTIFY THE MOST COST-EFFECTIVE METHODS TO PREVENT DAMAGE AND PROTECT RESOURCES FROM DAMAGE DURING CATASTROPHIC FIRE OR POST FIRE FLOOD EVENTS. THIS PROJECT ADDRESSES SHORTCOMINGS AND GAPS IN CURRENTLY AVAILABLE INFORMATION REGARDING RISK OF FIRE DAMAGE TO HISTORIC STRUCTURES AND ARCHEOLOGICAL SITES DURING AND AFTER WILDFIRES. THIS PROJECT WILL: 1) IDENTIFY WHICH SITES AND STRUCTURES ARE AT HIGH RISK OF FIRE DAMAGE BEFORE WILDFIRES OCCUR; 2) DEVELOP AN IN-FIELD TOOL THAT GIVES FIRE FIGHTERS AND ARCHEOLOGISTS ACCESS TO REAL-TIME INFORMATION ON FIRE RISK DURING A FIRE INCIDENT; AND, 3) IDENTIFY SITES AT RISK OF POST-FIRE FLOOD AND DEBRIS FLOWS AFTER FIRE. THROUGH THESE EFFORTS, WE WILL PROVIDE STANDARDIZE DATA INPUTS AND A TOOL TO CONDUCT RAPID SITE EVALUATIONS THAT ENSURE FIRE PREVENTION AND SUPPRESSION ACTIONS ARE IMPLEMENTED IN THE RIGHT PLACE AND AT THE RIGHT TIME. IN TURN, THIS WILL IMPROVE EFFECTIVENESS AND EFFICIENCY OF WORK AT CRITICAL INTERVENTION POINTS, BEFORE, DURING, AND AFTER WILDFIRE, TO FOCUS LIMITED RESOURCES ON THE HIGHEST PRIORITY AREAS. SUCCESSFUL IMPLEMENTATION WILL RESULT IN A ONE-OF-A-KIND DATABASE THAT LINKS INFORMATION FROM A RANGE OF SITE SURVEYS WITH FIRE INCIDENT, FIRE PREDICTION, AND POST-FIRE DATA. THIS DATABASE WILL PROVIDE INFORMATION THAT WILL BE FILTERED THROUGH A WEB ACCESSIBLE ASSESSMENT TOOL THAT PROVIDES REAL-TIME DATA ON FIRE RISK AND SITE PRIORITIES.

THIS PROJECT IS COMPRISED OF THREE INTEGRATED RESEARCH ELEMENTS DESIGNED TO GENERATE NEW INSIGHTS REGARDING THE DISTRIBUTION OF WILDFIRE RISKS AMONG COMMUNITIES, THE MECHANISMS THAT LEAD TO RISK EXPOSURE, AND THE ROLE OF COMMUNITY CHARACTERISTICS IN EXPLAINING THE ECONOMIC CONSEQUENCES OF WILDFIRE ACROSS THE SOUTHEAST COASTAL PLAIN STATES OF GEORGIA, FLORIDA, AND SOUTH CAROLINA (SECP). COLLECTING INFORMATION ABOUT WILDFIRE DAMAGE AND HOW IT AFFECTS ECONOMIC WELL-BEING IS ESSENTIAL TO AVOID A SUBSTANTIAL DECLINE IN THE CAPACITY TO RECOVER LOCAL ECONOMIC ACTIVITIES AND THUS IMPROVE COMMUNITY RESILIENCE. IF THIS RESEARCH IS NOT APPROVED, THE UNITED STATES DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURE FOREST SERVICE WOULD MISS AN OPPORTUNITY TO PROVIDE FACT-BASED INFORMATION THAT CAN ASSIST THE ADMINISTRATION'S EFFORTS TO PROMOTE MORE EFFICIENT AND LOCALLY RESPONSIVE DISASTER PREPAREDNESS AND RECOVERY PROGRAMS.

DISTURBANCES, SUCH AS WILDFIRES, INSECTS, DISEASE AND DROUGHT, ARE AFFECTING WESTERN FORESTS AND THE NATIONS ABILITY TO PRODUCE TIMBER. UNDERSTANDING HOW FORESTS RESPOND TO A RANGE OF MANAGEMENT OPTIONS AND DISTURBANCES IS CRITICAL TO CHOOSING THE RIGHT MANAGEMENT ACTION TO EFFICIENTLY ENHANCE TIMBER PRODUCTION. THE FOREST VEGETATION SIMULATOR IS A FOREST GROWTH MODEL THAT SIMULATES FOREST CHANGE IN TREE SURVIVAL AND GROWTH IN RESPONSE TO FOREST STAND DEVELOPMENT AND DISTURBANCES. THIS PROJECT WILL USE THE FOREST VEGETATION SIMULATOR TO ESTIMATE TIMBER PRODUCTION CONSIDERING DIFFERENT MANAGEMENT ACTIONS SO THAT THE BEST OPTION CAN BE CHOSEN TO ENHANCE TIMBER PRODUCTION. CALIBRATION OF THIS MODEL WILL IMPROVE ITS PERFORMANCE TO SPECIFIC FORESTS. THIS PROJECT WILL PROVIDE AN EASY-TO-USE FORMAT FOR THIS MODEL TO MORE EFFICIENTLY CHOOSE THE FOREST MANAGEMENT PRACTICES THAT WILL SUPPORT PRODUCTIVE AND HEALTHY FORESTS.OUTCOMES/DELIVERABLES:THIS PROJECT WILL ESTABLISH A PROCESS TO CALIBRATE THE FOREST VEGETATION SIMULATOR IN OREGON, SO THAT IT CAN EFFICIENTLY BE CALIBRATED FOR ALASKA, IDAHO, OREGON, WASHINGTON AND CALIFORNIA. THE COOPERATOR WILL ENGAGE WITH FOREST MANAGERS SO THAT THE PRODUCT ALIGNS WITH THEIR DECISION-MAKING PROCESS AND IS EASY TO USE. WEBINAR TUTORIALS WILL BE DEVELOPED FOR EACH STATE TO SHARE THE CALIBRATED TOOL AND FURTHER REFINE PRODUCTS SO THAT THEY ARE USEFUL AND USEABLE. THE PRODUCT WILL COVER ALASKA, IDAHO, OREGON, CALIFORNIA AND WASHINGTON AND DEVELOP A PLAN TO CONTINUE EXPANSION TO ADDITIONAL WESTERN STATES.

THIS PROJECT SUPPORTS RESEARCH TO UNDERSTAND HOW VALLEY RESET RESTORATION AFFECTS STREAM WATER TEMPERATURE OVER TIME. THE PURPOSE OF THE PROJECT IS TO DETERMINE WHETHER RESETTING STREAM CHANNELS AND RECONNECTING FLOODPLAINS CHANGES AVERAGE STREAM TEMPERATURES AND THE VARIETY OF TEMPERATURES WITHIN A STREAM ACROSS DIFFERENT SEASONS. THIS INFORMATION IS NEEDED BECAUSE ELEVATED STREAM TEMPERATURES ARE HARMFUL FOR FISH AND OTHER AQUATIC LIFE AND LIMIT THE EFFECTIVENESS OF RESTORATION INVESTMENTS. THE WORK WILL ALSO EXAMINE HOW RESTORED STREAMS RESPOND TO DISTURBANCE, SUCH AS WILDFIRE, BY COMPARING RESTORED AREAS WITH NEARBY UNRESTORED AREAS AFFECTED BY FIRE.IF THIS AWARD IS NOT APPROVED, LAND MANAGERS WILL LACK THE DATA NEEDED TO EVALUATE WHETHER VALLEY RESET IS AN EFFECTIVE TOOL FOR REDUCING HARMFUL STREAM TEMPERATURES. WITHOUT THIS INFORMATION, MANAGERS WILL BE FORCED TO RELY ON LIMITED OR SHORT-TERM STUDIES, INCREASING THE RISK THAT FUTURE RESTORATION INVESTMENTS FAIL TO IMPROVE WATER QUALITY OR AQUATIC HABITAT. THE AGENCY WILL ALSO MISS A CRITICAL OPPORTUNITY TO UNDERSTAND HOW RESTORED STREAMS RESPOND TO INCREASING WILDFIRE DISTURBANCE, LIMITING THE ABILITY TO ADAPT MANAGEMENT STRATEGIES UNDER CHANGING ENVIRONMENTAL CONDITIONS. WITHOUT CLEAR EVIDENCE ON WHICH RESTORATION PRACTICES IMPROVE THERMAL CONDITIONS, FARMERS, RANCHERS, PRODUCERS, LANDOWNERS, AND WATERSHED PARTNERS WILL FACE CONTINUED REGULATORY PRESSURE AND UNCERTAINTY, WHILE LACKING EFFECTIVE, PROVEN OPTIONS TO IMPROVE WATER QUALITY ON WORKING LANDS.
